# RiteSmith

> RiteSmith is the missing layer between LLM planning and deterministic execution.

## What it does

Most agent systems put the LLM in the critical path of every step — think, act, observe, repeat. RiteSmith breaks that loop:

- The **LLM / Agent** understands intent and submits it to RiteSmith
- **RiteSmith** searches existing artifacts; when something is missing, the LLM writes a short semantic plan that RiteSmith compiles into a Trama workflow (loops, joins, state and continuation are generated by code), plus strictly type-checked Luau scripts for missing logic. Artifacts are validated under guardrails (schema, types, tests, policy, sandbox) and registered in the artifact registry
- **Trama** executes the resulting workflow with retries, durable state, sleep, callbacks, compensation, and observability

RiteSmith is a **generator**, not an executor. It does not run workflows. Trama does.

## Core concepts

- **Intent** — a structured request submitted by an LLM or agent describing what needs to happen
- **Artifact registry** — the store of reusable Luau scripts and Trama workflow definitions that RiteSmith searches before generating new ones
- **Guardrails** — schema validation, policy checks, and sandbox execution that RiteSmith applies before registering any artifact
- **Workflow definition** — a declaristic description of steps, dependencies, and compensation logic that Trama can execute
- **Luau scripts** — sandboxed, strictly type-checked functions (LunarDyson runtime) that represent executable actions within a workflow
- **Semantic plan** — the compact description the LLM writes (calls, waits, conditions, parallel branches, bounded repeats); RiteSmith compiles it deterministically into a Trama workflow

## Measured generation cost (RiteSmith 0.2.1, October 2026)

Same 51-task corpus, gpt-5-mini at low effort, three runs per task; failures and repairs included:
- Workflows: 9,433 tokens and $0.0059 per valid workflow (was 22,482 and $0.0165), median 8.5 s (was 20.1 s), 68% valid (was 64%); valid = structural checks plus every argument and referenced field matching the capability contract
- Luau scripts: 3,011 tokens per valid script, median 5.7 s, 96% valid
- Execution in Trama uses no LLM tokens unless a workflow step calls an LLM capability
- Method: https://github.com/thiagoribeiro/ritesmith/blob/main/benchmarks/generation_latency/README.md

## What RiteSmith is not

- Not an LLM wrapper or prompt framework
- Not a workflow engine (Trama is the engine)
- Not an agent loop (it eliminates the loop)

## Relationship to Trama

RiteSmith is built on top of [Trama](https://trama.run), a lightweight saga orchestrator for reliable distributed workflows. Trama provides durable workflow state, retries, compensation, callbacks, and production-grade execution semantics.

## Links

- GitHub: https://github.com/thiagoribeiro/ritesmith
- Trama: https://trama.run (RiteSmith 0.2.1 requires Trama 3.0.1 or later)
